A creator showcases dozens of new and popular snacks and meals across the resort. It starts at the newly reopened Diamond Horseshoe lounge in Magic Kingdom, featuring Sweet Golden Corn Fritters (7/10), Glazed Sticky Ribs (8/10), Queso Fundido with BBQ Burnt Ends (8/10), Mini Churro Waffles (5/10), and a Charcuterie Platter (5/10). Other stops include Sunshine Seasons for a Plant-based Sofritas bowl (9/10), the Spring Roll Cart for Bacon, Egg, and Cheese Spring Rolls (9/10), and Outer Rim at Disney's Contemporary Resort for Elote Dip (9/10) and a charcuterie board (8/10). The tour heavily features Mickey-shaped waffles from All-Star Sports and other hotels — Caramel Banana (9/10), Strawberry (9/10), Birthday Cake (6/10), Candy Cereal (8/10), and Fruit Cereal (8/10) — plus multiple churro items like the Churro Overdrive (5/10), Churro-misu Cold Brew (6/10), Dole Whip Pineapple Sundae (8/10), EPCOT's Strawberry Shortcake Sundae (6/10), Bavarian Cream Filled Churros (4/10), and Cookies and Cream Mini Churros (9/10). Drinks highlighted include the Steamboat Willie milkshake (8/10), Golden Frozen Flame (4/10), S'mores Gelato Milkshake (8/10), Peaches and Cream (10/10), Orange Slushy Float (4/10), and Orange Bird Sunshine Twist (9/10). The video concludes by promoting a downloadable WDW Snacks Map.

description: This video is a promotional food segment about the 'mamposturria,' a viral fried snack originating in Caguas, Puerto Rico. Opening with a close-up of a hand holding the golden-brown, cylindrical fritter cut open to reveal its yellow plantain-based exterior and shredded meat-and-cheese filling, on-screen text announces '¡Desde Caguas! Se viraliza la sabrosa "mamposturria"'. The footage then shows the item being deep-fried in a commercial fryer basket until crispy, followed by gloved hands breaking it in half on a cutting board to display the interior texture. A plated version is shown garnished with microgreens alongside a dipping sauce. Chef Emanuel Ocasio, wearing a black apron with 'La Mancha de Plátano' branding, appears smiling while holding a wooden board of finished mamposturrias. The accompanying Spanish narration explains that the dish was created by Chef Ocasio as an experiment, consists of seasoned rice balls stuffed with meat and cheese, and that his restaurant prepares 2,000 to 3,500 by hand each week, with plans for a frozen version for Puerto Rican homes.

description: Two men are in a modern kitchen demonstrating how to make a high-protein, low-calorie homemade version of an Oreo McFlurry using a Ninja Creami machine. One man holds up a real McDonald's Oreo McFlurry while on-screen text states '300 CALORIES' for their version versus '810' for the McDonald's one, along with protein and sugar comparisons (23.3g protein / 7g sugar vs 18g protein / 92g sugar). They taste both, reacting positively to the homemade version, describing it as 'creamy' and 'thick.' The video then shows the recipe process: pouring ultra-filtered milk into the Creami pint, adding zero-calorie sweetener, a pinch of xanthan gum, and vanilla extract, mixing, freezing for at least 16 hours, then processing in the Ninja Creami. They add crushed Oreo cookies (shown being separated) and run the 'mix-in' cycle. The video ends with them tasting the finished product and giving each other a high-five, presenting it as a successful healthier alternative.
